unitTitle: Future Simple - Be going to - Present Continuous - Conditionals Type 1 - When/If

pairsWith.noteUz: Kelajak zamonlarni solishtirish, 1-tur shart gap, when/if nazariyasi + will/going to mashqlari.

scanNote:
GRAMMAR 2, 5-UNIT NAZARIYA DAVOMI + MAShQLAR (25-bet, PDF 24). Yuqorida o'ngda ko'k '5'.

Och pushti ramka:
• (be going to) for predictions based on what we see or know. 'Look at him. He's going to jump out of the train.'
'Future Simple - Be going to - Present Continuous' - 'Compare the examples.' 'She'll sell her bicycle. (she may or may not sell it.) He's going to study medicine next year. (intention) They're leaving for Cairo tomorrow. (fixed arrangement in the near future.)'
'Conditionals': • There are four types of conditionals. Each type consists of two parts: the if-clause (hypothesis), which begins with the word if, and the main clause, which shows the result of the hypothesis. if-clause (hypothesis) / main clause (result): 'If he wakes up late, he will miss the bus.'
'Type 1 Conditionals': Type 1 conditionals express a real or very probable situation in the present or future. They are formed as follows: if + present simple → future simple. 'If Tom studies hard → he will pass the exam.'
'When - if': • We use when in conditionals to show that we are sure that something will happen. 'I'll see you when I come to Paris. (I'm certain I'll come to Paris.)' • We use if in conditionals to show that we are not sure whether something will or will not happen. 'I'll see you if I come to Paris. (Perhaps I'll come to Paris, perhaps I won't.)'

PASTDA - 'Future Simple - Be going to':
1) 'Fill in the gaps with will/'ll and won't.' 1 A: I want to go camping next weekend at Blue Bird Lake. B: Who ...... drive you there? A: Tom's mother. B: Alright. But you ...... be careful, ...... you? 2 A: I need to go shopping. B: OK, I ...... give you a lift. A: That would be great. It ...... take me long, so afterwards we ...... have time to go for lunch. B: That sounds wonderful! 3 A: There's something wrong with Rocky. B: Oh, poor thing. I ...... take him to the vet. A: I ...... go with you. He ...... bark if I'm not there. B: I hope he ...... bite the vet! 4 A: I think I ...... have a barbecue at the weekend. B: That's a good idea. Who ...... you invite? A: I don't know yet. ...... you help me make a list? B: Of course.
2) 'Use the prompts and make sentences using will or be going to, as in the example.' 1 A: Look at the little boy! B: he/fall/swimming pool → He's going to fall into the swimming pool. 2 A: It's cold in here. B: I/turn on/heat 3 A: Mum, I'm hungry. B: I/make/you/sandwich 4 A: What are Maggie's plans for the summer? B: she/travel/Italy 5 A: Jimmy didn't study hard for his history exam. B: he/not pass/it 6 A: I have a headache. B: I/turn off/CD player 7 A: Dad, I don't feel well. B: I/take/you/doctor 8 A: Are you coming to Maria's party? B: yes/I/take/Jim/with me

Bet raqami: pastda o'ngda '25'.

exercises.instructionEn: Be going to is also used for predictions based on what we see or know: Look at him. He's going to jump out of the train. Compare: She'll sell her bicycle. (she may or may not sell it.) He's going to study medicine next year. (intention) They're leaving for Cairo tomorrow. (fixed arrangement in the near future.)
exercises.instructionUz: Be going to ko'rgan yoki bilgan narsaga asoslangan bashorat uchun ham ishlatiladi: Unga qara. U poyezddan sakramoqchi. Solishtiring: U velosipedini sotadi. (sotishi ham, sotmasligi ham mumkin) U keyingi yil tibbiyot o'qimoqchi. (niyat) Ular ertaga Qohiraga jo'nashadi. (yaqin kelajakdagi aniq kelishuv)
exercises.explanationUz:
UCh XIL KELAJAK - FARQI.

  WILL - fikrga asoslangan
    bashorat / noaniq:
    She'LL SELL her bicycle.
    (sotishi ham, sotmasligi ham
    mumkin)

  GOING TO - NIYAT yoki KO'RINIB
    TURGAN dalilga asoslangan
    bashorat:
    He'S GOING TO study medicine
    next year. (niyat)
    Look at him. He'S GOING TO jump
    out of the train. (ko'rinib
    turibdi)

  PRESENT CONTINUOUS - ANIQ
    KELIShUV (vaqt, joy belgilangan):
    They'RE LEAVING for Cairo
    tomorrow.


⚠ QISQAChA:

  will = o'ylayman
  going to = niyatim bor / ko'rib
    turibman
  -ing = kelishib qo'yganman

exercises.instructionUz: Shart gaplarning to'rt turi bor. Har biri ikki qismdan iborat: if-qism (shart, faraz) - 'if' bilan boshlanadi, va bosh gap - shartning natijasini ko'rsatadi: Agar u kech uyg'onsa (shart), avtobusga kech qoladi (natija). 1-tur shart gap hozir yoki kelajakdagi REAL yoki JUDA EHTIMOLIY vaziyatni bildiradi: if + present simple → future simple: Agar Tom qattiq o'qisa, imtihondan o'tadi. When - if: 'when' - biror narsa bo'lishiga IShONChIMIZ KOMIL bo'lganda: Parijga kelganimda seni ko'raman. (Albatta kelaman.) 'if' - bo'lish-bo'lmasligi NOANIQ bo'lganda: Parijga kelsam seni ko'raman. (Kelishim ham, kelmasligim ham mumkin.)
exercises.explanationUz:
1-TUR ShART GAP - REAL KELAJAK.

  IF + PRESENT SIMPLE, + WILL +
  FE'L

  If Tom STUDIES hard, he WILL
  PASS the exam.
  (shart)          (natija)

  ⚠ 'if' qismida 'will' YO'Q:
  'If Tom will study' ✗
  ⚠ O'zbekchada: '-sa' → 'if'.

  Ikki qism o'rin almashishi mumkin:
  He will pass the exam if he
  studies hard. (vergul yo'q)


WHEN va IF FARQI:

  WHEN = -ganda (ALBATTA bo'ladi):
    I'll see you WHEN I come to
    Paris. (Parijga albatta
    kelaman)

  IF = -sa (BALKI bo'ladi):
    I'll see you IF I come to
    Paris. (kelishim noaniq)

  ⚠ Ikkalasidan keyin ham PRESENT
  SIMPLE (will emas!).

exercises.instructionEn: Fill in the gaps with will/'ll and won't.
exercises.instructionUz: Bo'shliqlarni will/'ll va won't bilan to'ldiring.
exercises.explanationUz:
WILL / 'LL / WON'T.

  Savol: Who WILL drive?
  Question tag: you'll be careful,
    WON'T you?
  Qaror: I'LL give you a lift.
  Inkor: It WON'T take me long.
  Va'da/bashorat: we'LL have time;
    I'LL take him; I'LL go; He'LL
    bark; he WON'T bite
  Fikr: I think I'LL have a
    barbecue
  Savol: Who WILL you invite?
  Iltimos: WILL you help me?


⚠ 'TO GIVE SOMEONE A LIFT':

  = mashinada olib bormoq.


⚠ 'POOR THING':

  = bechora.

patterns.formula: If + KIM + FE'L(s), KIM + will + FE'L
patterns.exampleEn: If Tom studies hard, he will pass the exam. If he wakes up late, he will miss the bus.
patterns.exampleUz: Agar Tom qattiq o'qisa, imtihondan o'tadi. Agar u kech uyg'onsa, avtobusga kech qoladi.

patterns.formula: I'll see you when / if + KIM + FE'L(s)
patterns.exampleEn: I'll see you when I come to Paris. I'll see you if I come to Paris.
patterns.exampleUz: Parijga kelganimda seni ko'raman. Parijga kelsam seni ko'raman.

patterns.formula: Look at ...! KIM + is going to + FE'L
patterns.exampleEn: Look at the little boy! He's going to fall into the swimming pool.
patterns.exampleUz: Kichkina bolaga qara! U basseynga yiqilmoqchi.
